newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-based radio says broadcasts to China jammed.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-based radio says broadcasts to China jammed.

text.p: A U.S. government-financed radio station reported on Tuesday jamming to its Mandarin broadcasts to China, probably by the Chinese government.

Radio Free Asia, which began the Mandarin broadcasts in September 1996, said in a statement that the jamming began on Monday through the technique known as co-channeling -- broadcasting programs on top of the unwanted station.

"Despite the efforts of the Beijing government to prevent the Chinese people from hearing our broadcasts, we know that we are getting through, thanks to our multiple transmission sites throughout the Pacific Basin," it said.

Richard Richter, president of the radio station, said he was confident the Chinese authorities were behind it. "I can't imagine who else would do it. The Chinese have periodically jammed Voice of America broadcasts," he told Reuters.
The Mandarin broadcasts go out on about six frequencies. "There has been jamming on all but not on a constant basis. This seems to be the pattern with jamming," Richter added.

The International Broadcasting Bureau has also detected jamming to Radio Free Asia's broadcasts in the Korean and Vietnamese languages, the statement said. Richter said this started earlier than in the case of the Mandarin service.

The radio station says its mission is "to provide accurate and timely information, news and commentary ... and be a forum for a variety of opinions and voices from within Asian nations whose people do not fully enjoy freedom of expression".
